title: Answer: any system it feels like something to be, with the substrate left open and digital computers held out

statements.text: A system is conscious if and only if it feels like something to be it, and which objects and processes count toward consciousness is left open as the substrate problem. A frame-invariant theory should apply at non-human scales too, so qualia may lie well beyond the biological life of Earth. The later field account equates a first person perspective with a topologically bounded pocket of a physical field, most likely the brain's electromagnetic field, and holds classical digital computers incapable of creating causally significant experiences.
statements.scope: Principia Qualia (2016) and the field topology account of the boundary problem (2023 and later)

sources.locator: Synthesis: Eight Problems for a New Science of Consciousness, p. 22
